title: Legacy Data Extraction & ETL
tagline: Turn mainframe records, messy CSV exports and document text into clean, typed, reconciled data, and flag every value it could not trust.
why: Most enterprise AI projects stall on data, not models. The customer's truth lives in a COBOL system that exports EBCDIC files, in CSVs from five ERPs with five date formats, and in scanned PDFs. Before an agent can answer a question about an invoice, someone has to extract, normalize and reconcile that data, and prove the totals still match. This repo does those steps with exact decimal handling and an issue list instead of silent guesses.
covers: COBOL copybook parser: PIC X / 9 / S9 V9, COMP-3 packed decimal, COMP binary, zoned sign overpunch, OCCURS, FILLER, sequence columns
EBCDIC (code page 037) to Unicode, full 256-byte table
CSV cleanup: delimiter sniffing, RFC 4180 quotes, BOM, header names, US/EU dates, US/EU/accounting money, null markers, duplicate rows, per-row issue list
Reconciliation in integer cents: matches, amount breaks with tolerance, orphans both sides, duplicate keys, control totals
Labelled field extraction from OCR / PDF text with source line for each value and a missing-required list
gaps: No OCR engine or PDF parser here: feed it text from Tesseract, AWS Textract or pdftotext
No live mainframe connector (DB2 / IMS / VSAM over the network); it decodes the exported files
No Airflow or dbt project: each op is a pure step you can call from an Airflow task or a dbt Python model
Other EBCDIC code pages (e.g. 500, 1047) and COMP-1/COMP-2 floats

ops.label: Mainframe records
ops.help: Three 32-byte EBCDIC records from a VSAM export, decoded with the COBOL copybook. Balances are COMP-3 packed decimals (one is negative).

input.copybook:
* CUSTOMER MASTER - VSAM KSDS EXPORT
       01  CUST-MASTER.
           05  CUST-ID          PIC 9(6).
           05  CUST-NAME        PIC X(15).
           05  BALANCE          PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3.
           05  ORDERS-YTD       PIC S9(4) COMP.
           05  STATUS-CODE      PIC X(4).

ops.label: Messy CSV
ops.help: Semicolon delimiter, BOM, quoted delimiter, EU amounts, mixed date formats, a duplicate row and two bad values. Bad values stay as text and land in the issue list.

input.csv:
﻿Invoice #;Customer  Name;Inv Date;Amount
"INV-001";Acme Foods;03/04/2024;"1.250,00 EUR"
INV-002; Blue River Co ;Jan 5, 2024;(310,00)
INV-002; Blue River Co ;Jan 5, 2024;(310,00)
INV-003;"O'Neil; Sons";N/A;"2.000,5"
INV-004;Delta;31/13/2024;TBD

ops.label: Reconcile ledgers
ops.help: Mainframe ledger vs. new ERP. One rounding difference inside the 1-cent tolerance, one real break, one orphan each side.

ops.label: Fields from PDF text
ops.help: Text from an OCR pass over a scanned invoice. Each value has its source line. The PO number is required but absent, so it is reported, not guessed.

input.text:
NORDIC PARTS GmbH
Rechnung / Invoice
Invoice No.: NP-2024-00917
